pr_title: stm32: pwm driver enables complementary output for timer channel

issue_context.title: Cannot enable secondary pwm out channels on stm32f3
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
I face problems when trying to use the secondary pwm output channels on stm32f3_diso.
Inspecting the Pins shows no output, while primary channel is working.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. create an application using pwm output for stm32f3_disco rev E
2. use an overlay with the following content 
```
&pwm1 {
    pinctrl-0 = <&tim1_ch1_pa8 &tim1_ch2_pa9 &tim1_ch3_pa10 &tim1_ch4_pe14>;
    //pinctrl-0 = <&tim1_ch1n_pe8 &tim1_ch2n_pe10 &tim1_ch3n_pe12 &tim1_ch4_pe14>;
};
```
3. `west build --board=stm32f3_disco@E`
4. Flash and check PWM output
5. comment out first pinctrl line and uncomment second
6. Build and flash
7. Check PWM output on secondary pins -> not working

**Expected behavior**
The secondary pins should work the same way, the primary ones work.

Note: Inspecting the `TIM1_CCER` shows no difference, for both firmwares ( `0x1111` for both configurations,
while I expected `0x1444` for the second one, `x/xw 0x40012C20` in gdb)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Linux, Manjaro
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK 0.13.1
 - Commit SHA: 503b7e6f9ff07c2d340cefb6ae970495373e0153
comments:
I think like pinctrl already works correctly, but in `pwm_stm32_pin_set` cannot set the correct bits as [pwm_stm33.c#L262](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/5287ce8ff003f9ad7428864a9e53a42424b3d135/drivers/pwm/pwm_stm32.c#L262) can only select the ordinary pins.
So I would add another ch2ll like array, store which channels should use the N pin in the configuration and choose the array in .._pin_set from configuration. Did I miss anything?

It seems to be the key for this usecase, to add another  the ch2ll table of the pwm_stm32.c

```
+/** N output Channel to LL mapping. */
+static const uint32_t out_ch2ll[TIMER_MAX_CH] = {
+	LL_TIM_CHANNEL_CH1N, LL_TIM_CHANNEL_CH2N,
+	LL_TIM_CHANNEL_CH3N, LL_TIM_CHANNEL_CH4,
+#if TIMER_HAS_6CH
+	LL_TIM_CHANNEL_CH5, LL_TIM_CHANNEL_CH6
+#endif

```

Where `out_channel = out_ch2ll[pwm - 1u];` is the parameter for the following function call:
```
LL_TIM_CC_DisableChannel(cfg->timer, out_channel)
LL_TIM_CC_IsEnabledChannel
LL_TIM_OC_SetPolarity
```

The ./dts/bindings/pwm/st,stm32-pwm.yaml   defines the _period_ to be 

```
pwm-cells:
  - channel
# period in terms of nanoseconds
  - period
  - flags
```

also see the ./include/devicetree/pwms.h

Mainly used with PWM devices like in the drivers/led/led_pwm.c
```
#define LED_PWM(led_node_id)						\
{									\
	.dev		= DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_PWMS_CTLR(led_node_id)),	\
	.channel	= DT_PWMS_CHANNEL(led_node_id),			\
	.period		= DT_PHA_OR(led_node_id, pwms, period, 100000),	\
	.flags		= DT_PHA_OR(led_node_id, pwms, flags,		\
				    PWM_POLARITY_NORMAL),		\
},
```

It is not relevant in application like the ./samples/basic/blinky_pwm
